D018-D005_h001.question:
I’ve been struggling ever since that night during the armed robbery at my restaurant—three months ago now. I still hear the gunshots in my head, like they’re right there. If a car backfires or a plate drops, I jump—sometimes I drop things, my heart races, I can’t breathe. It’s like I’m back in that moment. I keep seeing the gunman’s face, even when my eyes are open. It’s not like I’m losing touch, but it feels so real—it’s part of what happened. These aren’t random voices or strange thoughts; it’s always *that* night.  

I love my husband, but I don’t feel it the way I used to. I can’t enjoy anything—the café, our dinners, nothing. I feel numb most of the time. And guilty. I keep thinking I should’ve stayed calm, should’ve done something differently. I get angry—at myself, at the world—like there’s a fire inside I can’t put out.  

Focusing on orders, staff schedules, even conversations—it’s hard. My mind’s always scanning, waiting for danger. But aside from reliving the trauma, I’m not hearing voices telling me things, and I know I’m not being watched for reasons beyond that night. This isn’t psychosis—it’s the aftermath of something real.
D018-D005_h001.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h002.question:
I’ve been struggling ever since the attack last year—someone broke into my apartment late one night. I wasn’t hurt physically, but I can’t shake it. Loud noises, even a car backfiring, make me jump so badly I sometimes drop things. I’ll hear a sound and suddenly feel like I’m back there, heart racing, breathless.  

I used to love my research, but now I don’t feel anything—no joy in my progress, no excitement when my advisor praises me. It’s like I’m numb. I keep thinking it wouldn’t have happened if my ex hadn’t ignored me that week—he knew I was anxious, and he just disappeared. I’m so angry all the time, even at little things. Sometimes I snap at my lab mates for no reason.  

My memory feels foggy—I’ll walk into a room and forget why, or misplace my notes constantly. And at night… I hear whispers, like someone’s moving in the hallway. But it’s not random—it’s always the same sounds from that night: keys jingling, footsteps. I know it’s not real, but it feels connected, like my mind keeps replaying it. It’s not like I’m seeing strangers or hearing voices about me—it’s only *that* moment, over and over.
D018-D005_h002.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h003.question:
I’ve been struggling ever since that explosion in the kitchen six months ago—I was right next to the deep fryer when it blew. I keep reliving it. Out of nowhere, I’ll feel the heat again, hear the blast, like I’m right back there. Sometimes someone brushes against me while I’m prepping food and I jump so hard I drop my knife—it scares everyone. My head feels foggy all the time, like I’m moving through water. I can’t enjoy things anymore. My wife tries, but I don’t feel anything, not even when we’re together. I keep thinking: *I should’ve seen it coming. I’m supposed to keep my team safe.* I feel ashamed—I run a station, I’m supposed to be in control. 

And sometimes… I see the cook on the ground, even when I’m not at work. But it’s not like I don’t know it’s a memory—it hits me because it’s *from* the event. It’s always the same image, tied to that moment. I’m not hearing voices or seeing things that aren’t connected. It’s just that day, over and over.
D018-D005_h003.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h004.question:
I’ve been struggling ever since the car accident last year—my husband was driving, and though I know it wasn’t his fault, I can’t stop thinking it should’ve been *him* who got hurt, not me. I keep reliving the moment: the screeching, the impact, the feeling of being trapped. It floods back out of nowhere, so vivid it’s like I’m there again, sometimes with sounds or even the smell of burnt rubber. I think that’s what the flashbacks are—these intense hallucinations, but they’re always about the crash, nothing else. 

I used to love my work as a speech therapist, connecting with kids, planning sessions—but now, I can’t get excited about anything. I cancel plans, avoid the garage where the car’s stored. Even picking what to wear or what to eat takes forever—I freeze up, overthinking every little choice. 

And when the dog barks or a door slams, my heart races, my hands shake, and it takes me ages to calm down. The hallucinations don’t come out of the blue—they’re tied to *that moment*. But otherwise, I know what’s real. I’m not hearing voices commenting on my life or seeing things unrelated. It’s just the accident, on repeat.
D018-D005_h004.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h005.question:
I’ve been struggling ever since that mugging last year—got jumped walking home late after coding. I keep reliving it, especially at night. I have these vivid dreams where I’m back there, heart pounding, trying to fight him off. Sometimes I wake up gasping, convinced he’s still here. The worst part is I can’t shake the guilt—I keep thinking I should’ve taken the main street, that I brought it on myself. I used to love gaming with friends, but now nothing feels fun anymore. I just feel… numb.

Lately, my focus at work has tanked. I keep forgetting where I left my keys, my phone—my team’s noticed how distracted I am. Any loud noise, like a keyboard slam or a server reboot alarm, makes me flinch hard. I saw a therapist who asked if I’d been hearing voices, and… yeah, sometimes I hear someone say my name right before something loud—like a distorted echo of that guy shouting during the attack. But it’s always tied to that moment. It’s not like I’m hearing random conversations or think anyone’s out to get me beyond that. It’s just… that night, over and over.
D018-D005_h005.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h006.question:
I’ve been struggling for over a year now—ever since I witnessed that terrible accident at the train station. I was on my way to work, and I can still see it: the impact, the noise. Some parts of that moment are just… gone from my memory, but other images won’t leave me alone. I avoid thinking about it—don’t talk about it, don’t go near trains—but sometimes, just hearing a loud sound makes my heart race, my hands shake. It’s like I’m back there.

I used to find comfort in things, but now I feel… hollow. My husband says I’ve changed—like I’m present but not really there. I get irritable so easily, even over small things like dishes or the TV volume. I’m always watching the door, jump if someone walks in suddenly.

And the dreams—sometimes I see him again, the man from the tracks. It’s not like voices or full hallucinations, but I *see* him in front of me for a second, like he’s right there. It’s always tied to that event, never random. It fades quickly, but it shakes me. I’m scared, but I don’t feel crazy—I know it’s part of what I saw. Nothing else feels distorted. I just can’t escape that memory, even though part of it still won’t come back.
D018-D005_h006.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h007.question:
I’ve been struggling since the car accident last year—hit by a drunk driver. Sometimes, out of nowhere, I’m back there: the headlights coming at me, the crushing sound. I’ll be on a sales call and suddenly I’m frozen, heart racing, like I’m reliving it. My husband says I zone out, call my name five times. I don’t remember it all—whole chunks of that night are just… gone.  

It’s hard to feel close to anyone now. I love my husband, I know I do, but I can’t *feel* it. Like my heart’s sealed off. I avoid talking about the crash, even with him. If someone brings up hospitals or ambulances, I get quiet, leave the room.  

Lately, I’ve snapped at colleagues over tiny things—spilled coffee, a delayed meeting. One time, a coworker walked up behind me fast, and I jumped so hard I dropped my laptop. I keep the blinds closed at home; sudden movements scare me.  

And those visions—when I see the truck lurch toward me—it’s not like imagining. It’s real. But only that moment, only the accident. I don’t hear voices, don’t think people are watching me. It’s *just* that crash, over and over.
D018-D005_h007.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h008.question:
I’ve been having these nightmares—over and over—about the accident. I’m back in the car, seeing my mom’s face right before the crash. I wake up sweating, heart racing, and sometimes I’m even yelling. It’s like I can’t escape it. I try not to think about that day, especially the moment I heard the glass shatter… I can remember pieces—her voice, the rain—but that split second when it happened? Nothing. It’s blank.  

I used to feel so close to my boyfriend, but now… I don’t know. I love him, but I can’t *feel* it. Like something inside just shut down. I avoid talking about it, avoid anything that reminds me—even driving past that stretch of road makes me panic. My chest tightens, I tremble, and I don’t settle for ages. Last week I snapped at my director during rehearsal—started screaming when he raised his voice. I felt terrible after, but in the moment, I just exploded.  

And sometimes… I see her. Not fully, but a flash—her hand reaching or her coat in the rearview. It’s not like I’m confused or losing touch, but I *know* it’s from the trauma. It’s always tied to that moment. Nothing else feels off—no voices, no paranoia. Just this… echo I can’t silence.
D018-D005_h008.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h009.question:
I’ve been having these terrifying episodes where I’m back in that alley—like I can smell the rain on the pavement, hear the shouts, feel the hands on me. It’s not just a memory; it’s like it’s happening all over again. They call them flashbacks, I think. I don’t talk about it—can’t. I’ve blocked out most of it, actually. Just… gone. My mind won’t let me go there. 

I feel empty a lot—like I’m watching life through a window. I used to love performing, but now everything feels fake, distant. I get jumpy—someone walks into a room too fast, and I’m on my feet before I even know why. It’s like my body’s always braced for another attack. 

And when I get angry—really angry—something snaps. I threw a chair across my apartment last week. No voices, nothing telling me to do it. But during flashbacks, it's like I *see* the guy who assaulted me. Not in my room now—but right then, in the memory, I *see* him. That’s the only time I see anything connected to the trauma. Other than that, it’s just me, trying not to feel anything.
D018-D005_h009.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h010.question:
I’ve been struggling ever since that armed robbery six months ago—when they held a gun to my head in the convenience store while I was buying snacks after work. I keep reliving it. Sometimes, out of nowhere, I’m back there—the flickering light, the smell of cigarettes, the cold metal. I’ll duck or flinch like it’s happening again. It’s not just a memory; it feels real. I avoid gas stations now. My wife noticed I won’t even drive down that street.

I remember the gun, the voice, but whole chunks are blank—like what he said right after. It frustrates me. I used to take pride in smashing my sales targets, but lately, even when I win an account, there’s nothing—just emptiness.

When I get startled, my heart hammers for ages. Last week, a car backfired and I was shaking for half an hour. My boss said I snapped at a client, and once, I threw my phone across the room. I don’t sleep. Sometimes, I hear his voice—whispering threats—but only when something triggers that memory. It’s always *his* voice, from that night. No other voices. Never see things or believe strange ideas. It’s just... him.
D018-D005_h010.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h011.question:
I’m the head nurse on a busy floor, so I need to be sharp—always have been. But since the accident last year, when a gunman got into the ER and I lost two of my team… I just can’t shake it. I keep *seeing* it. Out of nowhere, I’m back there—heart racing, the smell of blood, his voice. Just yesterday, a patient raised his hand quickly and I froze, convinced he was pulling a weapon. It’s like it’s happening all over again. I avoid the east wing, won’t go near the trauma bays unless forced, and I barely speak to the surviving staff. One of the techs from that night? Sarah. I hold her responsible—we were supposed to lock down, but she hesitated. If she’d acted, maybe it could’ve been contained.  

The world just feels… dangerous now. Like safety’s a lie. And I’ve been short-tempered—snapping at residents, yelling at administrators. It’s not like me. I’ve even heard the gunman’s voice when I’m alone—clear as day—telling me I failed. But I know it’s not real. It’s *his* voice—*that* moment. That’s all it ever is. Not voices commenting on me, not delusions about being controlled. Just the trauma. Over and over.
D018-D005_h011.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h012.question:
I’ve been having these awful episodes where I suddenly feel like I’m back in that terrible moment—during the war, when my husband and I were caught in the bombing. I see the smoke, hear the screams, and for a few seconds, I can’t tell it’s not happening right now. Sometimes I shout or crouch down, and my neighbor said I looked “a thousand miles away.” These aren’t dreams—they hit me in the middle of the day. I avoid the news, fireworks, even the subway entrance that looks like the shelter we used. I’ve stopped going to the senior center because the basement reminds me of it.

I keep thinking it was my fault—like if I’d left earlier, my husband would still be alive. The world feels so dangerous now, like it’s only a matter of time before something awful happens again. I get so jumpy that when my grandson startled me last week, I threw my teacup across the room. I don’t want to hurt anyone, but I can’t control the anger.

And yes, sometimes I hear my husband calling my name during these flashbacks—but only then. I know it’s not real. It’s always tied to that memory. I don’t hear voices other times, and I’m not confused about where I am. It’s just that moment… over and over.
D018-D005_h012.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h013.question:
I’ve been struggling for over a year now since... well, since what happened during that open house. I was alone in the property when someone broke in. I managed to hide, but I heard everything—his voice, the footsteps, the crash when he threw something. Ever since, any loud noise—even a door slamming in an empty house—sends my heart racing, and I can’t breathe right. Sometimes I even feel the same sweat on my palms, like I’m back there.

I don’t talk about it. I avoid thinking about it, but the memories just come—especially at night. I blame myself. I should’ve left earlier. Should’ve locked the doors. I keep thinking the world isn’t safe—nowhere is. I used to love showing homes, but now I see danger in every corner.

Sometimes, I hear that same voice—muttering the words he said. It’s like he’s right there. But I know it’s not real. It’s always *that* voice, *that* moment—never anything else. I haven’t seen monsters or strangers following me. It’s just him, just that night. And when the stress builds, I’ve thrown things—once shattered a lamp. I don’t know how to calm down anymore.
D018-D005_h013.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h014.question: I’ve been struggling ever since that armored truck exploded outside my office during a protest downtown—two years ago now. I still see the flames, hear the blast, feel the heat like it’s happening all over again. Sometimes, even the smell of burning trash sends me into a cold sweat, my heart slamming in my chest. I shut down emotionally, avoid talking about it, and I won’t even drive past that part of the city. Honestly, I’ve started believing the world’s just a cruel, unsafe place. I should’ve left work earlier that day—if I had, maybe I could’ve stayed clear. My wife says I’m not myself—I get angry easily, snap at her, threw a coffee mug against the wall last week. What really scares me is… sometimes I *see* the victim’s face in the corner of the room. Not just a memory—it’s like he’s standing there. But it’s always *him*, from *that moment*. It’s not random. I don’t hear voices telling me things or believe someone’s spying on me—I know it’s my trauma coming back, not my mind breaking entirely.
D018-D005_h014.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h015.question:
I’ve been struggling ever since the fire at the restaurant six months ago. I still see it—the flames, the smoke, my line cook trapped behind the pass. It just hits me outta nowhere, even while I’m prepping food. I’ll smell smoke and freeze, heart racing like I’m back in it. I don’t want to talk about it, not with my wife, not with anyone. Talking makes it feel real all over again.  

Since then, I keep thinking the world’s just cruel—like bad stuff’s always waiting. I should’ve shut the gas off sooner. I was distracted, joking around. That’s on me.  

At home, I’ve been short-fused. I yelled at my wife last week for nothing—just left the kitchen light on. I didn’t mean to, but it set me off.  

And… sometimes I hear him. My cook. Calling my name, telling me he can’t get out. It’s not like voices in my head—I *know* it’s not now—but in the moment, especially when I’m tired, it feels like I’m back there. It’s always the same—only that moment, nothing else. I don’t hear commands or secrets. It’s not like I’m losing touch. It’s like my brain won’t let me escape that night.
D018-D005_h015.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h016.question:
I’m a sound engineer, so I’m usually around loud environments, but lately, it’s been almost impossible for me to focus during sessions. About eight months ago, I was in a serious car accident—my fault, maybe, but I still can’t stop reliving it. I keep having these flashes—sudden, vivid memories of the impact, the sound of shattering glass, the scream. Sometimes it hits out of nowhere, and I’ll jump or drop whatever I’m holding.  

I’ve been avoiding anything that reminds me of it. I won’t drive, and if someone plays audio with screeching tires or loud crashes, I have to leave the room. I even had a fight with my best friend because I blamed him—he suggested I take that route that night. I know it’s not really on him, but it feels like someone has to be responsible.  

I’m always on edge, constantly checking exits, watching people’s movements, like I’m waiting for something bad to happen again. And… sometimes I hear the crash again, not like a memory—it’s like I’m back there, hearing it in real time. But it’s only that sound, nothing else. No voices, no paranoia—just the accident, over and over.
D018-D005_h016.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h017.question:
I’ve been having a hard time since the explosion at the plant two years ago—me and two other guys were right near the furnace when it happened. I wasn’t badly hurt, but one of them didn’t make it. Lately, just seeing a spark from a welder or hearing a loud bang sends me into a panic. My chest tightens, I can’t breathe right, and I keep reliving that moment—the screams, the smoke. I’ve started avoiding the shop floor altogether, even though it’s my job. I ask my team to send reports instead, and I stay in the office. 

I check the exits every time I walk into a room. In restaurants, I sit with my back to the wall, constantly watching people. It’s exhausting. I blame myself—those valves needed checking, and I signed off too fast. Maybe if I’d slowed down… 

And sometimes, it’s like I see him—standing there in full gear, face blackened. I hear his voice saying, “You let me die.” It only happens when something triggers the memory—never out of the blue. I don’t hear other voices or think people are after me. It’s always *that moment*—just replaying, like I’m back there.
D018-D005_h017.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h018.question:
I’ve been struggling for about six months now—ever since the break-in at my office. I was alone late that night auditing systems when someone smashed the window and came in. They didn’t touch me, but I was frozen, like I couldn’t move or scream. Since then, I keep reliving it—suddenly, right in the middle of a meeting or even while eating, I’ll see his face again, hear the glass shatter. It’s like it’s happening all over. I try not to think about it, but the harder I try, the more it comes back. I’ve stopped going to the office after hours, even though that’s when I get the most work done.  

I can’t help but think it’s the security team’s fault—like they ignored the risks we’d reported. If they’d acted, this wouldn’t have happened. I’m always watching now, even at home—checking locks, looking at shadows, listening. I can’t relax. And sometimes… I hear footsteps behind me when no one’s there. But it’s always *those* footsteps—the same as that night. It’s not like voices telling me things or seeing strangers—just echoes of *him*, tied to that moment. Nothing else feels disordered; I know it’s my mind replaying what happened, not something new.
D018-D005_h018.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h019.question:
I’ve been struggling ever since that workplace accident two years ago—when a press machine malfunctioned and killed one of my crew. I keep reliving it. Out of nowhere, I’ll see it happen again, like it’s playing in front of my eyes, especially when I’m near the line. That’s why I’ve stopped going to certain sections of the factory. I avoid the area entirely, don’t even like driving past the building on my days off. I can’t talk about it—not with my wife, not with coworkers. It just makes everything worse.

I blame the maintenance contractor. They cut corners. I know the company says it was mechanical failure, but if they’d done their job, Ramirez would still be alive. 

I’m always scanning now—checking exits the moment I walk into a room, watching people’s hands, their eyes. It’s like I’m waiting for the next thing to happen. And sometimes… sometimes I hear his voice calling my name right before it happened. It’s not like voices in my head generally—it’s always that moment, that same few seconds. It’s like I’m back there. But I’m not seeing things that aren’t there, and I know I’m not losing my mind. It’s just *that* scene I can’t escape.
D018-D005_h019.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h020.question:
I’ve been having these flashes—like sudden scenes—that come out of nowhere. I’ll be working on my thesis, and suddenly I’m back in that alley, reliving every sound, every second. It’s not just a memory; it feels like it’s happening again. I can’t stop it. Afterward, I’m shaky, nauseous, like I’ve been punched. I try not to think about it, but the more I push it away, the more it comes back. Sometimes I even avoid opening certain files on my laptop because a word or image might trigger it.

I keep asking myself why I took that short cut that night, why I didn’t fight harder—maybe it wouldn’t have happened. I don’t sleep much. When I’m out, I always sit facing the door, check the exits, scan faces. It helps… a little.

And sometimes—this is hard to say—I hear his voice when no one’s there. Not like conversations, just fragments, right before a flashback. It’s always the same words, the ones he said. I haven’t heard voices otherwise, and I know they’re not real, but they’re tied to *that moment*. It’s not like I’m losing touch with reality—I’m here. But that night keeps pulling me back. This has been going on since the assault, nearly eight months ago.
D018-D005_h020.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h021.question:
I’ve been struggling for over a year now—ever since that audit trip to Manila when the explosion happened near our hotel. I wasn’t injured, but I saw things… people screaming, blood… and ever since, it's like I can't shut it off. If I hear a loud noise or see flashing lights, I freeze up or start shaking. Even the smell of smoke from a barbecue triggers me. I feel… dirty, like I should’ve done something, should’ve helped. I can’t look my wife in the eye sometimes—I’m ashamed I walked away unscathed when others didn’t.

I don’t enjoy much anymore. My daughter got straight A’s last month, and I just nodded and said “good job,” but inside? Nothing. No pride, no joy. And at work, I snap. I yelled at a junior auditor last week for a minor typo—cursed him out. I’m not like that. But I can’t control it.

Sometimes… I see things. Like a flash—someone in a red shirt just at the edge of my vision, just like one of the victims. It’s always *that* moment, *that* scene. But I know it’s not real. There’s no voices, no paranoia—just these images, always tied to *that day*. They come and go, but they always bring me back there.
D018-D005_h021.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)

D018-D005_h022.question:
I’ve been struggling for years—ever since my time during the riots back in the 70s, when I was caught in that crowd and saw people get hurt. Lately, it’s like I’m back there. I keep having the same dream over and over—smoke, shouting, the feeling of being crushed—I wake up sweating, heart racing. It’s not just dreams, though. Sometimes during the day, out of nowhere, it hits me—the fear, the panic—like it’s happening all over again.

I can’t relax anymore. I’m always on edge, even at home. My wife says I jump at nothing. And I get angry—too angry. Last month, I threw a lamp when the grandkids were loud. I don’t want to hurt anyone, but it’s like something inside snaps.

I haven’t felt proud of anything in years, not even when my grandson graduated. Nothing feels meaningful. And… sometimes I hear voices—my name being called just like that officer did when I was trapped—but only then, only tied to that moment. It’s not like I’m hearing random voices every day. It’s always connected to *that day*. I know I’m not seeing things now, and I’m not paranoid—nothing else is wrong. It’s just that one memory, coming back.
D018-D005_h022.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)

D018-D005_h023.question:
I’m a PhD researcher, and lately, I’ve been struggling to focus on my work—even when I defend my thesis soon, it doesn’t feel like an achievement.
